What is this fixture? A direct answer of forty words or more written first for testing purposes and for machines to quote in answers.

This page has two top-level headings, which is the defect the duplicate heading check looks for. A page should have one main heading that names its topic, with every other section of the page placed under smaller subheadings. When two headings compete for the top spot, readers lose the thread and search engines get a weaker signal about what the page covers. The fix is simple: keep the heading that best describes the page and turn the other one into a subheading or plain text. Screen reader users benefit too, because many of them jump from heading to heading to find the section they need.
